_comment: Hand-curated list of generic UI-utility phrases that are page chrome rather than anything a business says about itself. Same pattern and rationale as page-type-keywords.json: a static file, not inline arrays, so the vocabulary is editable without a redeploy and reviewable as data. Matched against a normalised string (lowercased, punctuation and trailing counters stripped) at the parse layer, so every downstream field inherits the exclusion instead of each one re-filtering. Deliberately NOT a heuristic about tone or length — every entry here is a phrase that exists to operate the website, and the test for adding one is 'would this appear on a site selling anything at all'. Anything genuinely ambiguous is left OUT: 'shop all' and 'notify me' are real calls to action on a store, and excluding them to be safe would cost more than the noise does.
_exact_comment: Whole-string matches after normalisation. Safe because these are complete labels, never fragments of a sentence.
_contains_comment: Substring matches, reserved for banner and empty-state sentences that are unmistakable chrome even inside a longer block. Kept short on purpose: a substring rule is far easier to over-apply than an exact one, and a false positive here silently deletes real copy.
